title: 'The fun kid on the corner': Victim of police shooting in Collingwood remembered by friends
subtitle: Matthew Rice was 29.
article: The victim of a fatal police shooting in Collingwood on Sept. 9 is being remembered fondly by friends on social media.
Matthew Rice, 29, died after an incident involving police in the area of Third and Beech streets.
An obituary notice posted online said there was no formal service, but Rice was cremated.
"Matthew will be deeply missed by all those who loved him," the obituary read.
On the page, Vince Pinkey remembers spending time with Rice.
"I remember growing up with you ... back and forth from each other's houses gaming and sharing stories," he wrote. "I'm sorry we lost touch big guy, you'll always be in my heart."
Danielle Thompson said she will remember Rice as "the fun kid on the corner."
"Thinking about your family, may you rest in the sweetest paradise," she wrote on Facebook.
Katie Gill wrote on Facebook that she knew Rice since they were 10 years old.
"He was always a good kid," she said. "RIP to another friend gone too soon."

According to the province's Special Investigations Unit, officers responded to a report of a barricaded man at a residence on Third Street at about 12:30 p.m. As officers were setting up the perimeter, the man exited the residence. He was in possession of a firearm.
One officer deployed his conducted-energy weapon. When this proved ineffective, the same officer fired his gun and struck the man. He was transported to hospital, where he was pronounced deceased.
The SIU is an arm's-length agency that looks into reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
